title: Coherent compact-support reduction tower functor
statement:
Let $K_0$ be a field, $X,Y$ finite-type $K_0$-schemes, and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Fix a prime $\ell$ invertible in $K_0$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and put $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Use the small pro-etale sites and coefficient universes of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. For a scheme $W$ write $B_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_W$ for the completed coefficient sheaf [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], $\mathcal A_W=\operatorname{Mod}(B_W)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $D(\mathcal A_W)=D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A_Y)=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal A_Y)$ be the abelian category of strict inverse sequences, with compatible levelwise maps and levelwise exactness [def-weil-inverse-system, lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Choose one compactification $c=(j,p)$ of $f$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], and let $Rf^{c}_{!,n}=Rp_{*,n}j_!$ on $(A_n)$-module derived categories [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. For $K\in D(\mathcal A_X)$ let $K_n=K\otimes^L_{B_X}(A_n)_X$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction], and let $\operatorname{Res}_n$ be restriction of scalars along $B_Y\to(A_n)_Y$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], applied termwise to complexes; it is exact by [lem-weil-restriction-of-scalars-exact].

There is an exact $R$-linear functor lifting the composite of derived reduction, extension by zero along $j$, the separately derived proper direct image $Rp_*$, and restriction of coefficients, with the scalar action induced by the compatible constant sections $R\to\Gamma(W_{\mathrm{proet}},B_W)$:
$$
\mathcal T_f^c:D(\mathcal A_X)\longrightarrow D(\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A_Y))
$$
[def-weil-linear-functor, def-weil-triangulated-category]. Its $n$-th evaluation is naturally isomorphic to $\operatorname{Res}_nRf^{c}_{!,n}K_n$, including on morphisms. Under these identifications its transition from $n+1$ to $n$ is $\operatorname{Res}_{n+1}$ of $Rf^{c}_{!,n+1}$ applied to the quotient-induced map $K_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}^{A_{n+1}}_{A_n}K_n$, followed by the coefficient-restriction comparison of [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars] and $\operatorname{Res}_{n+1}\operatorname{Res}^{A_{n+1}}_{A_n}=\operatorname{Res}_n$. For every $m\geq n\geq1$ these identifications carry the composite transition from $m$ to $n$ to the map induced by $A_m\twoheadrightarrow A_n$ and the coefficient-restriction comparison; the identifications are natural in $K$.

proof.text: For each scheme $W$ put $C_{W,n}=(A_n)_W$ and let $\mathscr S_W$ be the category of semilinear coefficient systems in [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]: its objects have $C_{W,n}$-modules $M_n$ and $C_{W,n+1}$-linear maps $M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}M_n$. Here is a simultaneous ringed-site realization. Take $\mathcal V_W=W_{\mathrm{proet}}\times\mathbf N_{\ge1}$ with arrows $(V,k)\to(U,n)$ given by $V\to U$ and $k\le n$, and coverings at fixed index. The underlying topos is the inverse-sequence topos of [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. The ring sheaf $C_W$ has value $C_W(U,n)=C_{W,n}(U)$, with restrictions the quotient homomorphisms followed by site restriction. Unpacking the module-sheaf definition [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] identifies $\operatorname{Mod}_{\mathcal V_W}(C_W)$ with $\mathscr S_W$; the sheaf condition at $(U,n)$ is exactly the sheaf condition at level $n$. Kernels and cokernels are componentwise, and [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] applies to this small ringed site. Thus its unbounded derived category is available with simultaneous K-injective resolutions. The constant-sequence functor from sheaves on $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ is exact and left adjoint to limit: a map from a constant sequence is exactly a compatible family of maps. It therefore gives a morphism of topoi $\pi_W:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal V_W)\to\operatorname{Sh}(W_{\mathrm{proet}})$, with ring map $\pi_W^{-1}B_W\to C_W$ furnished by all the limit projections $B_W\to C_{W,n}$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] to the ringed morphism $\pi_X$ from step 1. This gives an exact functor $\mathcal R_X=L\pi_X^*:D(B_X)\to D(\mathscr S_X)$. Choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to K$, which exists by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The same pullback theorem computes $\mathcal R_XK$ by the single strict system of complexes $P\otimes_{B_X}C_{X,n}$: its transition for $m\ge n$ is $\mathrm{id}_P\otimes q_{m,n}$, where $q_{m,n}:C_{X,m}\to C_{X,n}$ is the coefficient quotient. This evaluates to the derived reduction $K_n$ of [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction]. For $m\ge n\ge k$, the chain-map identity $(\mathrm{id}_P\otimes q_{n,k})(\mathrm{id}_P\otimes q_{m,n})=\mathrm{id}_P\otimes q_{m,k}$ holds before localization. The pullback theorem gives natural comparisons for maps of resolutions, so this constructs a functor on derived morphisms and retains the strict quotient composition identities, rather than choosing a lift of a diagram in the ordinary derived category.

proof.text: Let $\overline X$ denote the middle scheme of the chosen compactification. The pro-etale morphisms induced by $j$ and $p$ are those of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. For each $n$, [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] identifies $u^{-1}C_{W,n}$ with $C_{V,n}$ for $u:V\to W$ equal to $j$ or $p$. These identifications preserve all quotient maps: both composites on a constant section $a\in A_m$ give its image in $A_n$, and the maps of constant sheaves are uniquely determined by these sections. Thus the coefficient systems satisfy the inverse-image hypothesis of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. For $j$, [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies its site with the slice site. The extension theorem [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] gives exact $j_!$ at each coefficient; for each quotient $A_m\to A_n$, the identification $j_!\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}=\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}j_!$ is explicitly part of [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars], applied to the chosen compactification. It leaves the underlying additive sheaf and maps unchanged, with the scalar action restricted. These compatible levelwise extensions form an exact functor $J:\mathscr S_X\to\mathscr S_{\overline X}$. Write $J_D$ for its exact derived descent. On the same system categories define $P^{-1,\mathscr S}$ by levelwise $p^{-1}$ and $P_*^{\mathscr S}$ by levelwise $p_*$. The compatible coefficient identifications just checked make these functors on semilinear systems. Their componentwise adjunction bijections restrict to compatible families: naturality of the unit and counit identifies the transition-commutativity condition on either side. Thus $P^{-1,\mathscr S}\dashv P_*^{\mathscr S}$, with exact left adjoint because inverse image and system exactness are componentwise. Let $RP_*^{\mathscr S}$ be the total right derived functor computed using a K-injective resolution of the entire system. The simultaneous-section theorem [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] supplies its natural evaluation identifications with the separately derived $Rp_{*,n}$, on objects and morphisms, together with the coefficient comparisons and their composition homotopies. We apply the geometric inverse-image/right-adjoint and open-extension clauses of that theorem, which hold for every semilinear section, including the possibly noncartesian output of $J_D$. The added cartesian-first-input hypothesis in its fiberwise internal-Hom clause has no role in this composite of derived reduction, open extension and proper direct image. This is an application to the separately derived proper functor after $J_D$.

proof.text: Define $U_Y:\mathscr S_Y\to\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A_Y)$ by restricting the scalar action at level $n$ along $B_Y\to C_{Y,n}$. The transition is $B_Y$-linear because $q_{m,n}\pi_m=\pi_n$. The underlying additive sheaves, kernels and cokernels are unchanged, so $U_Y$ is exact, as in [lem-weil-restriction-of-scalars-exact]. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] it descends to an exact functor $(U_Y)_D$ on unbounded derived categories. Set $\mathcal T_f^c=(U_Y)_D\circ RP_*^{\mathscr S}\circ J_D\circ\mathcal R_X$. Step 2 and the evaluation identifications of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] now give natural isomorphisms $\operatorname{ev}_n\mathcal T_f^c K\cong\operatorname{Res}_n Rp_{*,n}j_!K_n=\operatorname{Res}_n Rf^c_{!,n}K_n$, where the last equality is the composite definition in [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. Every displayed identification is between functors, so it also identifies their maps on arbitrary derived morphisms.

proof.text: The four factors defining $\mathcal T_f^c$ are triangulated. This holds for $\mathcal R_X$ by the exact derived pullback theorem in step 2 and for $J_D$ and $(U_Y)_D$ by exact descent in steps 3-4. For $RP_*^{\mathscr S}$, the source and target are module categories on the small ringed system sites of step 1, so [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] supplies K-injectives in the required unbounded categories. The additive functor $P_*^{\mathscr S}$ therefore has a triangulated right derived functor by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-triangulated-functor-composite] successively proves exactness of the displayed composite with its composite shift isomorphism. This proves exactness in the actual derived system/tower category.

proof.text:
Write $F_n=Rf^c_{!,n}$, and write $d_{m,n}:K_m\to\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}K_n$ for the map in step 2. Let $\chi_{m,n}:F_m\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}F_n$ be the specified comparison of [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars], applied to $A_m\twoheadrightarrow A_n$. Under the simultaneous-section model of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], $J_D$ carries $d_{m,n}$ to $j_!d_{m,n}$ and its right derived direct image carries this to $Rp_{*,m}(j_!d_{m,n})$ followed by the direct-image coefficient comparison. The latter is the canonical derived adjunction comparison: the cited section theorem specifies it by the derived counit transpose and preserves adjunction transposes on evaluation. The normalization can also be checked against [lem-weil-proetale-direct-image-restriction-of-scalars]: for a K-injective $C_{\overline X,n}$-complex $I$ and a K-injective replacement $\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}I\to H$ over $C_{\overline X,m}$, its direct-image comparison is the inverse of $p_*\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}I=\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}p_*I\to p_*H$. The adjunction comparison has this normalization: its composite with that replacement map is the identity after localization, by naturality of the derived counit and the adjunction triangle identity. Hence it is that same inverse, with no assumption that $\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}I$ is K-injective. Here the simultaneous-section theorem supplies the coefficient-projection comparison as a coherent map on arbitrary sections; its invertibility is supplied separately by [lem-weil-proetale-direct-image-restriction-of-scalars]. Thus this use stays within the current theorem's geometric-comparison clause and its stated scope. The compact-support comparison $\chi_{m,n}$ is precisely the composite of that direct-image comparison and the underlying identity $j_!\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}=\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}j_!$, as stated in [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars]. Hence the resulting tower transition is
$$t_{m,n}=\operatorname{Res}_m\bigl(\chi_{m,n,K_n}\circ F_m(d_{m,n})\bigr),$$
with $\operatorname{Res}_m\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}=\operatorname{Res}_n$. At $m=n+1$ this is exactly the transition required by the statement; it is natural in $K$ because all its constituents are natural maps in the cited system construction.

proof.text:
For $m\ge n\ge k$, write $\chi_{a,b,L}:F_a(\operatorname{Res}_{a,b}L)\to\operatorname{Res}_{a,b}F_b(L)$, so its input $L$ is a complex over $A_b$. Before final restriction to $B_Y$, the composite transition has source $F_mK_m$, target $\operatorname{Res}_{m,k}F_kK_k$, and is
$$\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}(\chi_{n,k,K_k})\circ\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}F_n(d_{n,k})\circ\chi_{m,n,K_n}\circ F_m(d_{m,n}).$$
Naturality at the $A_n$-linear map $d_{n,k}:K_n\to\operatorname{Res}_{n,k}K_k$ gives
$$\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}F_n(d_{n,k})\circ\chi_{m,n,K_n}=\chi_{m,n,\operatorname{Res}_{n,k}K_k}\circ F_m(\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}d_{n,k}).$$
The transitivity clause of [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars] gives
$$\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}(\chi_{n,k,K_k})\circ\chi_{m,n,\operatorname{Res}_{n,k}K_k}=\chi_{m,k,K_k}.$$
Substitution therefore identifies the composite with
$$\chi_{m,k,K_k}\circ F_m\bigl(\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}(d_{n,k})\circ d_{m,n}\bigr)=\chi_{m,k,K_k}\circ F_m(d_{m,k}),$$
where the last equality is the quotient chain-map identity in step 2. Applying $\operatorname{Res}_m$ gives $t_{n,k}t_{m,n}=t_{m,k}$. Identity quotients give identity transitions. Induction on $m-n$ identifies every composite of successive transitions with the single quotient-induced map in step 6. The section model in [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] retains these composition identities and their homotopies throughout; this calculation identifies their evaluated maps and never infers equality of derived system maps from equality of their evaluations.

proof.text: Finally the scalar $r\in R$ acts on the entire coefficient system by the compatible constant sections $r\bmod\varpi^n$, and on $B_W$ by their inverse-limit section. At the complex level, tensor pullback sends multiplication by $r$ to multiplication by its image, since $(rx)\otimes a=x\otimes(ra)$; extension by zero and coefficient restriction keep that multiplication on their underlying additive sheaves; direct image sends the same sheaf map to itself on sections. The derived constructions retain these identities: on K-flat representatives the first identity is the same tensor formula, and on K-injective representatives multiplication by $r$ is the actual chain map $r\,\mathrm{id}$. The bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] identifies it with its derived morphism, so computing the right derived functor sends it to $r\,\mathrm{id}$. Resolution comparison maps are module maps, hence commute with these scalar endomorphisms, as do their inverses after localization. These are identities on the system complexes, not only at individual levels. Each factor is additive (exact/triangulated by the earlier steps), and therefore for a morphism $a:K\to L$ one has $\mathcal T_f^c(ra)=\mathcal T_f^c((r\,\mathrm{id}_L)a)=r\mathcal T_f^c(a)$. Together with additivity this is precisely $R$-linearity [def-weil-linear-functor].
